title: Gradient Clipping and Stability knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes “Gradient norms” in this lesson?
options: This topic guarantees identical results across all devices and package versions.
This topic makes every serialized checkpoint safe to load from an unknown source.
Identify the value being differentiated and the scalar objective; compare the resulting gradient with a tiny analytical or numerical check.
This topic removes the need to validate inputs or inspect model outputs.
questions.answer_key: Identify the value being differentiated and the scalar objective; compare the resulting gradient with a tiny analytical or numerical check.
questions.explanation: Gradient norms: Identify the value being differentiated and the scalar objective; compare the resulting gradient with a tiny analytical or numerical check.

questions.prompt: Before relying on “Clipping by value”, what should a learner verify?
options: Skip recording package versions because they cannot affect API or device behavior.
confirm model and input devices match, supported dtype/device combinations are used, and the measured result is numerically acceptable.
Assume all tensor dimensions and devices are interchangeable without checking them.
Use the held-out test split repeatedly to tune the model and report that score as unbiased.
questions.answer_key: confirm model and input devices match, supported dtype/device combinations are used, and the measured result is numerically acceptable.
questions.explanation: This lesson recommends the following check: confirm model and input devices match, supported dtype/device combinations are used, and the measured result is numerically acceptable.

questions.prompt: Which pitfall matters when applying “Clipping by norm”?
options: Do not treat a GPU availability check as proof that all model operators or precision modes are supported.
Change several unrelated settings at once and infer which change fixed the result.
Treat successful imports as proof that the full model and evaluation pipeline are correct.
Catch every exception and silently replace failed results with zeros.
questions.answer_key: Do not treat a GPU availability check as proof that all model operators or precision modes are supported.
questions.explanation: This topic-specific caution is important: Do not treat a GPU availability check as proof that all model operators or precision modes are supported.
